issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify that Animal.messageOnFeed() returns a String (and the exercise examples expect String messages like "Oink!", "Maah!", "Arf Arf!"), but the solution repository defines Animal.messageOnFeed() to return a FeedResponse object (and provides a FeedResponse class). This return-type divergence is a structural mismatch: students following the specification will implement messageOnFeed() returning String, while the solution uses a custom FeedResponse type. This inconsistency can confuse students about the required method signature and will prevent direct substitution between student code and the provided solution/reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the return type across artifacts. Either: (A) Change the solution to match the problem statement by making Animal.messageOnFeed() return String and update all subclasses (Seal, Pig, Goat) to return the specified String messages; remove or adapt the FeedResponse class. Or (B) Update the problem statement and UML to explicitly document and teach the FeedResponse type (i.e., specify messageOnFeed(): FeedResponse and describe the FeedResponse class), so students are instructed to implement the FeedResponse-based API. Prefer option A to match the current exercise description and UML.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Animal.messageOnFeed() as returning a String, but the solution repository changes this conceptual entity by introducing a FeedResponse class and declaring Animal.messageOnFeed() to return FeedResponse. Furthermore, individual animal implementations are inconsistent (e.g., Goat.messageOnFeed() returns String while Pig and Seal return FeedResponse). This mismatch between the expected String message and the FeedResponse wrapper (and the inconsistent returns across subclasses) creates confusion for students mapping the specification to the provided solution and template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation of the animal feed message consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to align with the problem statement by having Animal.messageOnFeed() return String and remove the FeedResponse class (update Pig/Seal/Goat to return Strings), or (B) update the problem statement and template to document the FeedResponse type and require messageOnFeed() to return FeedResponse consistently (and ensure all animal subclasses return FeedResponse). Prefer option A to match the original UML and instructional text.
